Alex — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and the items we agreed to follow up on: 

Recap (my notes)
- Use-case: clinical note summarization + triage classification (short prompts, ~500 tokens/profile).
- Expected traffic: initial pilot 100k users/mo, avg 3 requests/user => ~300k requests/mo.
- Typical context window: 1.2k tokens (prompt + response), so estimate ~360M tokens/mo.

Pricing signal you mentioned on the call
- Procurement target: "$X per 1M tokens" (you said internal goal is in the low double digits).
- Preference for predictable billing (monthly commit) to unlock better unit economics.

Follow-ups from Redwood
1) Quick competitive mapping: we’ll show a $/1M tokens comparison vs OpenAI, Anthropic, and a representative open-host (estimated).
2) Suggest target pricing tiers for a committed pilot (30d commit / 6mo ramp).
3) Provide a short attachment with run-rate math and modeled unit cost assumptions (attached).

Ask from you
- Can you confirm the internal target $/1M token range (even a rough band like $10–$25)?
- Any procurement constraints (PO timeline, legal review windows) we should plan for?

I attached an initial runbook (medicore_token_runbook_v1.xlsx) — it contains the simple token math and two pricing scenarios (hosted vs dedicated). I’ll circulate a short competitive table in my next email.

Best,
Ben

Ben — thanks for the clear recap and the spreadsheet. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Target band: procurement has a preferred target of $12–$18 / 1M tokens for pilot purchases. That’s what gets budget approved internally for POC work. If we can hit ~"mid-teens" with a commit, it’s much easier to move forward.

2) Expected volumes: the 360M tokens/mo number aligns with our internal estimates; we expect 3–6x growth if the pilot shows lift. For procurement sizing assume a 12-month smoothing.

3) Benchmarks we’re using
- OpenAI (gpt-4.1-like hosted): ~ $40–$60 / 1M tokens for instruction-style generation in our past quotes.
- Anthropic: ~ $30–$50 / 1M tokens depending on context length and SLO.
- Open-model hosts (3rd party): we’ve seen $15–$22 / 1M tokens (varies by SLA and quantization).

4) Legal/procurement notes: we need a standard SOW + a short security questionnaire answered (SOC2 scope, retention, region). Timeline: Procurement review window is 2–3 weeks; legal another 1–2 weeks.

Next steps from our side: I’ll share the official volume + expected API call distribution and loop in our security contact. Would appreciate a host-comparison table with Redwood’s recommended target $/1M for (a) no-commit hosted, (b) 6mo commit, (c) dedicated GPU reserved.

—Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: post-demo cost targets & host comparisons

Alex — perfect, that target band helps a lot. Attaching a short host-compare summary inline here and a proposed commercial for pilot. Quick highlights below: 

Redwood host-comparison (illustrative $/1M tokens)
- No-commit hosted: $28 / 1M tokens (managed; includes 99th pct latency SLO, streaming)
- 6mo commit (pilot): $16 / 1M tokens (volume-based discount, predictable capacity)
- Dedicated reserved (12mo): $10 / 1M tokens (reserved GPU pool; best unit economics, optional on-prem pricing varies)

Notes on assumptions
- We assumed your token mix (50% prompt, 50% response) and 1.2k avg context.
- Savings to reach the $10 reserved assumption require a 12mo commit and ~1.2TB KV cache locality (reduces per-token compute).
- Open-model hosts often achieve lower list prices but with weaker SLOs and limited observability (so effective cost can be higher due to retries/backoff).

Proposed pilot commercial (example)
- Duration: 6 months
- Commit: 200M tokens/mo guaranteed; overage at $18 / 1M tokens
- Onboarding credit: first month 50% off
- Security: we’ll provide SOC2 controls summary and a short answers pack by next Wednesday.

If that fits the $12–$18 band you shared, we can draft an SOW and price sheet for procurement to review. Can you confirm:
- Do you need a PO before we start the SOW?
- Who on your side will own the security questionnaire (I can coordinate directly to speed review).

I’m looping Marissa (customer success) to own onboarding timeline. Laura is on commercial approvals for the discount language.

Thanks — Ben
